By Nathan Bomey · Nov 19, 2026

Thursday ✅. Anthropic's much-anticipated journey to the public markets is complete.

Today's newsletter is 890 words, a 3.5-minute read.

📉 The dashboard: The S&P 500 closed down 2%, its sixth straight session in the red — its longest losing streak since 2024.

🥶 Today's stock spotlight: AMD (-7.7%) fell after Hunterbrook Media reported that the chips giant is heavily exposed to potential U.S. chip export restrictions, prompting its affiliated hedge fund to short the stock.
 
 
1 big thing: 🐜 ANTi up
 

CEO Dario Amodei and other Anthropic executives ring the opening bell at the Nasdaq in New York. Photo: Charly Triballeau/ AFP via Getty Images
 

Anthropic opened for trading just before noon today in one of the biggest public stock offerings ever.

📈 By the numbers: ANT shares closed at $97.17, a gain of 17% from yesterday's IPO price of $83.

  • But they slid nearly 13% from where they opened trading at $111.50.
  • Aided by an early surge in retail buying, they rose to a high of $115.10 before retreating. They fell as low as $92.72 just after 1:15pm.
Data: Financial Modeling Prep; Chart: Erin Davis/Axios

The impact: Enthusiasm for the first major pure-play AI model developer to hit the stock market wasn't enough to shake the larger cloud hanging over the AI trade.

  • The PHLX Semiconductor index closed down another 2.4% today, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite shed 2.4% as well.

🗣️ What they're saying: "What the debut offers is a read on demand for frontier AI exposure at scale and a public filing against which the business can now be measured," tech analyst Dan Ives said.

💸 Follow the money: Anthropic ultimately raised $81.3 billion from the IPO and another $26 billion from a private placement, marking the largest stock sale ever.

The bottom line: Investors ultimately couldn't resist the promise of a company that says its technology is so powerful that it could destroy humanity.
 
 
2. Consumer checkup
 

Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios
 

Walmart raised its sales and earnings outlook as its online business continues to surge.

  • Why it matters: The retailer is a bellwether for the broader economy, offering a window into the health of the American consumer.

🗣️ What they're saying: "The words we would use to describe the customer are stable, resilient," CEO John Furner said on this morning's earnings call.

In the U.S., customer transactions — excluding the fuel pump — rose 1.5% in comparable channels in the quarter ended Oct. 31 compared to a year earlier.

  • The average size of those tickets increased 1.4%.
  • Market share gains in grocery categories were some of the highest the company has seen in three years.
  • Upper-income households drove share gains across categories.

💻 The intrigue: eCommerce sales grew 17% in the quarter, and now represent 24% of Walmart's sales.

📊 Zoom out: The retailer posted $188.8 billion revenue for the quarter, up 5.2% from a year earlier and topping S&P Capital IQ expectations of $187.2 billion.

  • It also increased its fiscal year guidance for net sales from a previous range of up 4%-5% to a new range of up 4.9%-5.2%.

📉 Yes, but: The rate of comparable sales growth slowed in its Walmart U.S. division.

  • U.S. comp sales, which include online sales and sales at stores open at least a year, rose 2.9% in the quarter excluding fuel, down from 4.5% in the same period a year earlier.
  • 💊 The company noted that its pharmacy business took a significant hit from Medicare drug price negotiations.

Shares closed down 1% today, but are still up over 25% for the year.

4. 🕔 After hours: GTA flu outbreak
 

Grand Theft Auto VI is advertised for sale at a game store in Hong Kong today. Photo: Vernon Yuen/Nexpher Images via Getty Images
 

The initial reviews for Grand Theft Auto VI — released early this morning and expected to be the biggest entertainment hit of the year — are rolling in ... and they're breathless.

🗣️ A sampling:

  • NYT: It "largely lives up to its sky-high expectations by inverting the series's reputation for destruction."
  • WaPo: "It is a great gathering of art forms and talent, an unruly, comprehensive cultural atlas of American life and manners."
  • IGN: "I see no real limit to the amount of time I could spend here, endlessly exploring and interacting with Vice City and the massive area surrounding it."
  • The Verge: "The buildup to Grand Theft Auto VI's launch is unlike anything the game industry has ever seen. Even more remarkable? The game was actually worth the wait."

💰 By the numbers: The publicly traded Take-Two Interactive — which makes GTA through its Rockstar Games unit — got about 20 million pre-orders for the game, according to HSBC Global Investment Research analyst Mohammed Khallouf.

  • Khallouf today raised his 2027 GTA sales forecast from 40 million units to 52 million.

🤒 The bottom line: If you called in sick with the "GTA flu" to play the game today, you have company.

  • Silicon Valley company Logitech provided a new floating holiday for workers to play video games — and about 70% of one manager's entire team took it today, per NYT.
